provider: OVHcloud Public Cloud - GPU instances (self-managed VM): Quadro RTX 5000 16GB at USD 0.60/h, Tesla V100 16GB at USD 0.77/h (legacy t1 range; V100S exists too)
region_dc: Gravelines, France (GRA5/GRA7/GRA9/GRA11). Per GPU tracker (checked 18 Oct 2026) GPU instances also exist in London, Frankfurt, Warsaw. V100/V100S documented in GRA7, GRA9, GRA11, BHS5; which exact region currently offers Quadro RTX 5000 stock is [uncertain] (check live control panel).
sovereignty_class: EU HQ (Roubaix, FR) + EU DC: full EU corporate sovereignty, no US parent so no direct CLOUD Act exposure at corporate level. Certifications: ISO 27001 (cloud services), SOC 2 Type II; SecNumCloud/HDS/BSI C5 apply to specific offers, not verified for GPU instances [uncertain].
monthly_cost: FX assumed USD 1 = EUR 0.92 [uncertain]. Hourly 24/7 (730 h): RTX 5000 ~USD 438 (~EUR 403); V100 ~USD 562 (~EUR 517). Both are 2.7-3.5x over the EUR 150 cap. Monthly billing is documented as ~50% cheaper than hourly: ~EUR 200 (RTX 5000) / ~EUR 258 (V100), still over cap; whether GPU instances get monthly billing is [uncertain]. Savings Plans (1-36 months) exist, discount for GPU flavors unverified [uncertain]. POC hours (per-second billing): 50 h ~EUR 28 (RTX 5000) / ~EUR 35 (V100); 100 h ~EUR 55 / ~EUR 71. Break-even for EUR 150 cap: ~270 h/mo (RTX 5000), ~210 h/mo (V100). Add disk (~USD 0.05/GB/mo classic block) [uncertain: flavor local disk].
billing_granularity: Per-second hourly billing (1 minute minimum), meter starts at ACTIVE. Not scale-to-zero: stopped/paused instance is still billed at full rate; only delete (or shelve, snapshot-only billing on hourly instances) stops the cost. Monthly option is prepaid per commenced month, no proration on early delete.
setup_fee_and_lockin: No setup fee on hourly. USD 30 credit charge for first Public Cloud project (account funding check). Monthly billing = commenced month billed even if deleted; Savings Plans lock 1-36 months. Exit cost low: plain Linux VM plus GGUF file; snapshot/volume egress free.
gen_tps_7b_q4: [uncertain] Bandwidth-derived, not measured. RTX 5000 (Turing, 448 GB/s): ceiling ~100 t/s on 4.4 GB weights, realistic ~55-70 t/s. V100 (HBM2, 900 GB/s): ceiling ~200 t/s, realistic ~100-130 t/s in llama.cpp CUDA.
prefill_tps: [uncertain] Compute-derived estimate, not measured. RTX 5000 (~11 TFLOPS FP32, tensor cores): ~1800-2800 t/s PP for 7B Q4_K_M. V100 (125 TFLOPS tensor FP16): ~2500-4000 t/s. No FlashAttention-2 native on Volta/Turing in some paths, llama.cpp CUDA FA works on both.
ttft_at_4k: [uncertain] Derived from prefill estimates: RTX 5000 ~1.5-2.3 s; V100 ~1.0-1.6 s at 4k prompt tokens (warm, model resident, plus prompt cache can cut repeated tool-schema prefill to near zero).
concurrency_slots: [uncertain] 16 GB VRAM minus 4.5 GB weights leaves ~10-11 GB for KV/buffers. Mistral-7B-class GQA (8 KV heads) ~0.125 GB per 1k tokens at f16: -np 4 at 16k ctx each ~8 GB fits; -np 2-4 sensible. Compute not VRAM bounds throughput.
ctx_ram_headroom: 16 GB VRAM: 4.5 GB model + ~10 GB KV => 32k ctx fits single slot (~4 GB f16 KV), 64k+ feasible with q8 KV; practical limit is Bielik native context (version dependent [uncertain]). Instance vCPU/RAM sizes of the RTX 5000 flavor not verified [uncertain].
availability_status: Self-serve on demand via Public Cloud project, no waitlist documented. Stock per region/flavor varies and some GPU flavors need quota request [uncertain]. RTX 5000 / V100 are legacy GPUs; OVH lists newer L4 (USD 1/h, 24GB), L40S in GRA11. Check live panel for stock.
egress_traffic: Instance network traffic is not billed (OVH docs: bandwidth for instances is not billed; free outbound except Asia-Pacific beyond 1 TB/mo and S3 egress). Agentic traffic negligible.
electricity_metering: Not applicable (cloud, power bundled in hourly price). For reference: RTX 5000 ~230 W TDP, V100 PCIe ~250-300 W.
hosting_model: Self-host: raw GPU VM, you install NVIDIA driver, CUDA, llama.cpp server and manage Bielik GGUF Q4_K_M. Full control of chat template, --jinja flags and tool-call parser. Not a managed API.
tool_calling_support: Depends on own llama.cpp build: llama-server --jinja gives OpenAI-compatible /v1/chat/completions with server-side tool-call parsing for supported templates. Bielik template/parser compatibility must be validated [uncertain].
spec_decode_support: Yes in principle: llama.cpp supports a draft model (-md) on same GPU; 16 GB has room for 7B target plus small draft. Bielik DFlash draft compatibility with llama.cpp not verified [uncertain].
sla_uptime: OVH GPU page lists 99.99% SLA per GPU tracker (published SLA; applies to instance availability, credit-based) [uncertain exact scope for legacy GPU flavors].
llm_inference_tos: No restriction found; GPU instances marketed for AI/ML/inference. Standard OVH acceptable-use applies.
price_stability: Prices quoted in USD on us/world pages, EUR on EU pages; trackers show no change in last week (14-21 Oct 2026). Legacy range (t1/t2) price page shows t1-45 USD 0.77/h unchanged for long [uncertain historical changes]. Risk: legacy Turing/Volta GPUs may be retired in favor of L4/L40S.
model_lock_in: None: you bring own GGUF, nothing in a catalog to be removed (Bielik removed from OVH AI Endpoints catalog is irrelevant for self-host). Platform lock-in low.
